key_insight: Uncertainty in pulsatile coronary flow affects oscillatory and multidirectional wall-shear metrics more strongly than time-averaged wall shear stress.
engineering_relevance: Quantifying input uncertainty can help contextualize patient-specific coronary hemodynamic predictions and prioritize measurements that reduce prediction variability.
method: Use principal component analysis to characterize velocity-waveform variability.
Propagate uncertain velocity, pressure, viscosity, density, and heart rate through unsteady finite-element simulations using polynomial chaos expansion.
Apply global sensitivity analysis to separate individual parameter effects from interactions.
evidence_signal: Across three patient-specific geometries and 505 models per patient, fourth-order PCE emulators converged; median coefficients of variation were 0.15–0.20 for time-averaged WSS, 0.54–0.75 for oscillatory shear index, and 0.28–0.38 for cross-flow index.
watch_item: Evaluation covered only three patients; broader generalizability and clinical predictive accuracy remain unestablished in the abstract.
paper_title: Uncertainty Quantification and Global Sensitivity Analysis of Patient-Specific Coronary Hemodynamics Under Unsteady Flow Conditions
